fields.value: Machine-readable output and meaningful exit codes on every etude command

Give every `etude` command an output a program can parse and an exit code that says what happened, so a coding agent can drive Etude without reading prose.

## Why

Etude's main caller is increasingly a coding agent: it launches runs, checks on them, reads logs and decides what to do next. Jack Heart, 2026-11-13, on "the command line and docs are written for coding agents as much as for people": "100% this". On filing this: "This is probably a nice isolated task".

Today the roughly forty commands print text for a person, and no command offers a JSON form (checked at EXP-56 `105abdd`: `status`, `history`, `wait`, `logs`, `machines`, `pools`, `availability`, `usage` and the rest in `src/etude/launch/cli.py`; `report`, `checkpoints`, `sync` in `src/etude/cli.py`). Exit codes are documented in places only: 1 for a failed smoke, 75 for a planned stop.

## Outcome

* Every command that reports state has a machine-readable form whose fields are the public record types Etude already defines, not a second schema.
* Every command's exit code distinguishes at least: success, refused before anything was spent, failed, and stopped-but-resumable. The codes are listed in one place in the docs.
* Errors a program must act on carry a stable code (Etude already has names such as `experiment_not_named`) in the machine-readable form.
* An agent can do the common loop with no text parsing: launch, wait, read status and spend, read where logs and checkpoints are, cancel or continue.
* The docs say how an agent should call Etude, in a form an agent will find.

## Constraints

* Human output stays as readable as it is; this adds a form, it does not replace one.
* No new server or service; this is the SDK's command line.
* Agree with EXP-57 (live view) and EXP-58 (machines and metrics) on field names for what they add, so their data is machine-readable from the start.
* Keep commands fast: help and simple reads must not load heavy dependencies.

## Not in scope

A formal experiment record, budgets across launches of one experiment, and questions or findings belong to the hosted product, not this Task. In the SDK an experiment is a name runs share.
